beta_daily_stats.frequency: daily (Yahoo adj. close, run in Colab)

consensus.note: The base case is built to land on consensus for FY27–FY28, so any gap to the Street's targets comes from valuation, not from the near-term forecast. GAAP EPS here excludes equity-investment fair-value gains, which added about $1.08 to the FY27 GAAP guide.

history.quarter_note: Q3 FY27E is company guidance. Q1–Q2 FY26 segment figures are derived from reported year-on-year growth rates.
history.annual_note: Operating cash flow understates cash generation while Dell Financial Services grows: H1 FY27 CFO of $6.3B is after a $6.4B increase in customer financing receivables. The model values DFS separately at net book and keeps its debt out of WACC.

bridge_note: DFS (Dell Financial Services) is valued inside operations: its results are in ISG and CSG segment operating income, so its receivables are not added and its debt is not deducted. The reported DFS balances are kept in bridge_dfs_reported.

notes.segments: FY27 segment split: H1 actuals plus H2 implied by the $192B revenue and $74B AI-server guidance. FY26 AI vs traditional split is estimated from Q4 FY26 disclosures.
notes.operating: Margins calibrated to H1 FY27: ISG 12.9% (AI ~9%, core ~17%), CSG 7.8%, corporate 1.2%. Marginal NWC −7% matches the Jan→Jul 2026 balance-sheet change per dollar of added revenue.
notes.comps: Trailing EBITDA and sales flatter a company growing 69% this year, which is why forward P/E carries the most information here.
notes.rm: Default Rm = 10Y yield + Damodaran implied ERP (5.10% + 4.23% = 9.33%). Replace with your own expected S&P 500 return.
notes.beta: Daily regression vs S&P 500, Oct-2024 to Oct-2026 (n=500): beta 1.993, robust to weekly data, earnings days and April 2025. WACC uses the adjusted beta 0.67*1.993+0.33 = 1.665.

bridge.dfs_debt: 0 here; DFS debt (9,618, Q2 FY27 10-Q) is also left out of 'Debt excluding leases' because the DFS business it funds is valued inside operating income. Alternative: deduct it too (−$14.9 a share).
